disposition_reason: Master's dissertation (ITAL 2020) whose Chapter 2 is the manuscript later published as Ferreira de Oliveira et al. 2021 (Food Control 119:107455): same 90 bean samples, same regional Table 2, same single-batch processing results and Table 4 exposure scenario. All tables are extracted here, each finding tagged 'same samples as oliveira2021 Table 2' (or §3.3) so they are not double-counted.
disposition_locator: Ch.2 §2.1 (printed p.45, PDF p.59), Tabela 2 (printed p.52), §3.3 (printed p.55–57)

study.design: farm-batch survey plus single pilot-scale processing study (master's dissertation, Ch.2)
study.material_scope: fermented and dried cocoa beans (homogenized with shell); pilot-derived shell, liquor, cocoa powder, cocoa butter
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Beans grown in Brazil (Bahia, Pará, Espírito Santo, Rondônia), Côte d'Ivoire and Ecuador; acquisition channel not described beyond 'provenientes de diferentes locais de origem'; analysed in Campinas, Brazil
study.sampling_unit: batch of fermented and dried beans (thesis does not restate 'same farm'; journal says one batch per farm)
study.method: Dry ashing (450 °C, 15 h) then ICP OES (Agilent 5100 VDV, Cd 214.439 nm, Pb 220.353 nm); microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion evaluated as alternative
study.lod_loq: Cd LOD 0.0005 mg/kg, LOQ 0.0015 mg/kg; Pb LOD 0.007 mg/kg, LOQ 0.022 mg/kg (Tabela 1B)
study.basis: as analysed (beans with shell); no dry-weight or moisture basis stated
study.qa: CRM INCT-TL-1 Tea Leaves: Cd 103 ± 14%, Pb 86 ± 9% (dry ashing); NIST 1547 Peach Leaves: Cd 104 ± 9%, Pb 90 ± 5%; CV Cd 3%, Pb 6% (n=6)

controls.control: Pilot-scale processing partition of Cd (roast, crush, winnow, grind to liquor, press)
controls.design: processing study (single pilot batch, no replication)
controls.outcome: Cd shell 0.124 ± 0.004; liquor 0.060 ± 0.006 (-47% vs beans); cocoa powder 0.111 ± 0.010 (-2% vs beans; ~1.85x liquor); cocoa butter <0.0015 mg/kg. Pb: shell 0.142 ± 0.006, liquor/powder/butter <0.022 mg/kg (bean Pb for this batch not reported).
controls.scale: pilot (2 kg beans; 500 g liquor pressed)

controls.control: Cd mass balance across grinding and pressing
controls.comparator: total Cd mass entering each step

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary calls butter 'not detected at 0.0015' and partly notes the LOQ issue; primary prints 'não detectado <0,0015' which equals the LOQ, not the LOD (0.0005).
Stored summary (and journal) do not mention that the thesis obtains cocoa powder by sieving the cake ('peneiração'), whereas the journal says cake grinding.
Stored summary says thesis is open-access institutional; not verifiable from primary text (no licence statement inspected).
Stored summary describes beans as 'homogenized with shell' — consistent with primary §2.1.
unresolved: Collection period of the 90 bean samples is not reported anywhere in the thesis.

Per-sample values are only shown graphically (Figura 1 box plots, printed p.53); not digitized. The PA box plot visibly shows ~2 points above 0.3 mg/kg Cd while text/table state 3 PA samples (10%) exceeded 0.3 mg/kg; cannot reconcile from the figure.
Pb concentration of the starting beans used in the pilot processing is not reported; Pb partition could not be computed.
Treatment of <LOQ results in regional means (Bahia, Côte d'Ivoire, Rondônia, Ecuador) is not described.
Exposure section: thesis states Germany-consumption scenario reaches 395% of the PTMI for children; the journal prints 398%.
